# Long-Term Portfolio Experiment

> Web visualization of a long-term buy & hold investment experiment started in March 2016 with £100,000 of simulated capital (paper trading), built on fundamental and macroeconomic analysis. Site created by Agustín Díaz-Cano. MIT license.

## What it is

A long-term (hold) experiment: positions were bought in March 2016 using fundamental analysis, macroeconomic context and other factors, and left untouched for over a decade without active trading. The goal is to observe how a portfolio built on conviction evolves, without reacting to short-term noise. It does not use systematic trading techniques such as Turtle Trading: it is fundamental and macro analysis only.

## Data source

The analyzed portfolio is public and available on La Bolsa Virtual (profile marcelogallardiola): https://www.labolsavirtual.com/marcelogallardiola
It contains all the 2016 evidence transactions, unmodified. This site only visualizes it; it is not the author of the original portfolio and does not modify it.

## Positions

Gold, Crude Oil, JP Morgan Chase, Facebook (Meta), Alibaba, First Solar, Tesla Motors, Google (Alphabet), Starbucks, Silver, Amazon.com, Apple, NortonLifeLock (Symantec), Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Natural Gas (commodity).

## Account status (October 2026)

The platform reports in pounds (£); this site shows everything in US dollars.
- Initial capital: £100,000 (about US$142,700 at the February 2016 GBP/USD rate)
- Account value: £603,875.93 (about US$807,700 at today's rate), roughly 5.7x in USD terms
- Invested capital: £555,144.32 · Available capital: £42,363.51 · Balance: £48,731.61
- Margin used: £6,368.09 · Commissions paid: £422.18

Over the same period (same starting capital, in USD): S&P 500 total return about 4.7x, Berkshire Hathaway about 4.1x.

## The Tesla case

The Tesla position was taken when short interest in the stock hit an all-time record and market consensus was betting against the company. According to the project context, its market cap has grown from ~US$34 billion in 2016 to ~US$1.48 trillion today (roughly 43x).

## What the site shows

- Explanation of the experiment and the data source.
- Account performance indicators in US dollars.
- Historical chart (Feb 2016 to today) of the portfolio vs the S&P 500 (total return) and Berkshire Hathaway, as US$ value or indexed to 100, with per-asset overlay.
- Pie chart of the composition, by asset or by sector.
- Dark (default) and light mode.

## How the data is built

The portfolio is rebuilt from the 64 public transactions (22 Feb – 7 Apr 2016) with daily prices and FX from Yahoo Finance (stock splits applied, GBP converted to USD at each date's rate). A GitHub Action refreshes the data daily; if the remote data is unavailable, the last committed snapshot is used. The modelled value is within about 1% of the value reported by the platform. Caveat: the platform did not apply the 2022 Alphabet split to the Google position, and the site reproduces it as reported. Educational project: not investment advice.
